title: Greatest Common Divisor
domain: Nonnegative integers only: a >= 0 and b >= 0.
description: Compute the greatest common divisor of two nonnegative integers using Euclid's algorithm. This first Glon implementation uses repeated subtraction.
attribution: Challenge family: REBOL Cookbook / Rosetta Code. Problem definition: Rosetta Code, 'Greatest common divisor' (https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Greatest_common_divisor). The Glon implementation is original for this challenge.
reference: Expected values are independent Euclidean GCD results, checked against the mathematical definition gcd(a,b) = largest positive integer dividing both; gcd(0,0) is defined here as 0 to match the recursion base case.

cases.reference: The implementation's base case returns 0 for gcd(0, 0).

resource_probes.note: Largest tested subtraction chain that completed on the pinned 64K interpreter.
Known implementation limit, not a catchable SIN!. The program needs one recursive call per subtraction.

known_limitations: Accepts nonnegative integers only. Negative inputs are outside the contract and are not tested.
Subtractive Euclid uses one recursive call per subtraction. With the pinned 64K interpreter, gcd(73,1) succeeds while gcd(74,1) fail-stops with return-stack exhaustion.
The fail-stop is a machine-level halt, not a SIN!, so judge cannot catch it.
The recursion limit is an implementation resource limit; it is not worked around by changing the runtime in this challenge.
